newsitem.title: INDONESIA: IMF sees Indonesia economy slowing in 1996.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees Indonesia economy slowing in 1996.

text.p: International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus said on Thursday he expected Indonesia's economic growth this year to be lower than the 8.07 percent posted in 1995.

"I believe that the economic growth of your country this year will probably be below the very high performance achieved last year. I hear that the government expects 7.5 percent growth performance this year," Michel Camdessus told a news conference.
He said Indonesia needed to continue making its market more flexible to keep economic growth at a high level.
"Seven percent or 7.5 percent is already a high rate of growth sustainable in the medium term and (will) contribute to reduce the problem of unemployment," he said.

Camdessus, in Jakarta for a two-day Southeast Asian economic meeting, said Indonesia was facing a high current account deficit but prudent macroeconomic policies by the government would help tackle the problem.

"I believe...by deepening and continuing the present approach of prudent macroeconomic and monetary policies, your government will avoid seeing such a current account deficit from becoming a worrying factor," he said.

Indonesia expects its current account deficit to widen to $8.7 billion in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March), or about four percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), from $7 billion, or about 3.2 percent of GDP, in 1995/96.
